fichas.title: Energy Saving Regulation and Thermal Insulation
fichas.summary: Summarizes EnEV 2007 requirements for energy assessment of residential and non-residential buildings. Assessment considers primary energy demand for heating, hot water, ventilation, cooling and, for non-residential buildings, lighting. For new residential buildings, the envelope-area process considers the ratio of heat-transmitting area to heated building volume and uses a monthly balance procedure.

fichas.title: Thermal Insulation Design of Stairwells
fichas.summary: For thermal insulation design, a temperature of at least 15°C can be assumed for stairwells. Radiators may be needed in the lower stairwell to ensure this temperature.

dimensions.label: Assumed stairwell temperature
dimensions.context: Minimum temperature assumed for thermal insulation design of stairwells; may need to be ensured with radiators in the lower stairwell.
dimensions.ocr_raw: a temperature of ≥15°C can be assumed

fichas.title: Design Values of Building Products
fichas.summary: Explains how energetic characteristics of building products are used to determine U-values for thermal insulation verification. Design values are obtained from relevant standards or approvals; nominal values are converted for temperature, moisture and ageing. The text specifies a partial safety factor for the thermal conductivity of insulation materials.
uses: Establish design values for building products

dimensions.label: Partial safety factor for thermal conductivity
dimensions.context: Applied to nominal thermal-conductivity values of thermal insulation materials.
dimensions.ocr_raw: a partial safety factor of γ = 1.2

fichas.title: Sun Protection and Summer Heat Verification
fichas.summary: Summer heat protection must be verified under EnEV 2007. The permissible sun input depends on factors including glazing energy transmission, window orientation and inclination, frame proportion, shading effectiveness, facade window area, climate and effective thermal capacity. The room-related sun input factor must not exceed the maximum permissible factor.

fichas.title: Wind, Airtightness and Thermal Bridges
fichas.summary: EnEV 2007 requires the heat-transmitting envelope, including joints, to be permanently airtight. Mechanical ventilation calculations may account for heat recovery or reduced air-change rates only when airtightness is verified; ventilation systems must allow users to influence airflow. Thermal bridges can increase heat loss and create low surface temperatures, condensation and mould risk; they may be accounted for by adjusting U-values or through separate verification.
uses: Reduce heat loss and condensation risk
